atoms.b: Theatre was an ((++important irrelevant)) part of ancient Greek life, with the Dionysus Theatre in ((++Athens London)) being the oldest.
Built in the 6th century ((++BC CB)), it’s considered to be the birthplace of drama.
The origins of theatre lie in a religious festival, which was ((++held cancelled)) to honour the god Dionysus.
The opening day started with ((++choir karaoke)) singing and was followed by several days of competition for the ((++best worst)) play.

trainers.instruction: At the end of the festival, the best plays were rewarded. Listen and match each prize with the correct description.

b.sound: The playwrights were crowned with a laurel wreath.
The playwrights received sacrificial animals as a prize.
A banquet was held in honour of the winning plays.

feedback.end: Ancient Greek actors wore masks with exaggerated facial expressions to help the audience easily understand the different characters and emotions.

atoms.text: There were two main types of plays that were performed: comedies and tragedies.
Comedies were funny and often mocked men in power. Tragedies usually ended in a sad or disastrous way for the main character.
Sophocles, a famous playwright, wrote many well-known tragedies that are still performed today.

trainers.instruction: Listen and decide whether the following situations belong to a comedy or a tragedy.

atoms.sound: a character gets caught in a funny love triangle
the play makes fun of a political figure
a family suffers from a curse of the gods
at the end, the main character loses everything
